fields.statement: QA at cafec91c with a scratch build of ./cmd/rhiza in a scratch git repo (real git, fake rex and claude on PATH, RHIZA_* run env unset). run start --workflow plan --new X <cs> exits 2 'takes no change set'; --workflow build --new X exits 2 'workflow "build" is not plan'; --milestone without --new exits 2; none opened a change set or a run. With RHIZA_TEST_NOW/SEED fixed, --dry-run --json predicted change 01M6A6FYW86T3BKSK9V4MCGPCP and wrote nothing; the real run (--permission-mode manual) opened that same ID as a draft intention 'Plan reports', made it current, created worktree repo.plan-reports on cs/plan-reports, started the agent with 'Plan 01M6A6FYW86T3BKSK9V4MCGPCP', and the run journal's change field named it. --new ... --milestone opened a draft record. With RHIZA_SESSION set the start is refused (exit 2) and no draft is left behind.

QA at cafec91c: ran the scratch build's `rhiza tui app roadmap` in a 200x40 pty with a logging fake rex on PATH. m shows 'Intent of the new milestone: _', typed Go and enter show 'Start an interactive plan run of a new milestone "Go" in a new Rex tab? y/n', y makes one call `rex window new -s session:qa new-milestone -c <repo> --json -- <rhiza> run start --workflow plan --new Go --milestone` with no change set argument, and the app stays open saying 'Opened Rex tab running the plan run of a new "Go"'. n gives new-change-set and no --milestone; backspace edits the text (Shipx then backspace gave --new Ship). Empty enter, esc at the intent prompt, and n or esc at y/n made no call. Works on an empty roadmap. Seen: the tab's run start carries no --permission-mode, so with the built-in plan workflow it exits 2 in the tab ('agent step with no permission mode') before opening a draft. The existing p key has the same gap. Raised as a discovered-from draft change set.

QA at cafec91c: `rhiza guide plan` from the scratch build prints the new step-2 text for an intention change set that serves no intent yet. Followed it by hand on the draft that run start --new opened: change show --json gave "serves": []; added an intent with rhiza apply, then ran the guide's exact `rhiza link <cs> serves <intent> --change <cs>`; change show --json then listed that intent's ID under serves.
